findings.title: Translation cache key ignores fallback locales, so cached fallback strings go stale when default_locale changes
findings.body: With the new fallback chain (user locale -> SiteSetting.default_locale -> :en), the value returned for I18n.t(key) under a given locale now depends not only on that locale's YAML file but also on SiteSetting.default_locale. However, the LRU cache key in I18n.translate is built as "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}", which does not include the fallback locales. SiteSetting.default_locale is a runtime-changeable setting (admins can change it from the site settings UI without a restart or I18n.reload!), so after such a change, requests for a key missing in the user's locale will keep serving the previously cached string from the OLD default locale until the cache is cleared. The cache key (or the cache invalidation) needs to account for the fallback list.

findings.title: Fallback locales are only preloaded in the web request path; background jobs and mailers get broken fallbacks
findings.body: The translate accelerator only lazy-loads I18n.config.locale inside I18n.translate (lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb line 68: load_locale(config.locale)). When the Fallbacks backend resolves a miss by looking up the key in the default locale or :en, those locales' YAML files are never loaded by that code path. The PR compensates for this by calling I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! in ApplicationController#set_locale, but that before_filter only runs for web requests. In background jobs and mailers (e.g. user-targeted emails where I18n.locale is set to the recipient's locale), the fallback locale files are not loaded, so fallback lookups will miss and produce 'translation missing' strings (or the raw missing-translation marker) instead of falling back to the default/English text. The preloading should happen wherever locale is switched, or the accelerator should load the fallback locales for config.locale inside translate/load_locale.

findings.title: No tests for the new fallback behavior
findings.body: This PR introduces a nontrivial behavior: a custom FallbackLocaleList whose [] computes [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en] on every lookup, a per-request ensure_loaded! in ApplicationController#set_locale, and interaction between fallbacks and the caching/lazy-loading translate accelerator. None of this is covered by tests. At minimum there should be specs verifying that (a) a key missing in the user's locale is served from the site default locale and then :en, (b) the fallback order is correct when locales coincide, and (c) the accelerator still caches correctly across locales. Without these, regressions in translation resolution (e.g. from future i18n gem upgrades or changes to the accelerator) will ship silently.

findings.title: Fallbacks are now enabled in development and test, masking missing-translation errors
findings.body: Previously `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` was only set in production, profile, and the cloud66 production config; development and test ran without fallbacks, so a missing key in a locale file surfaced as a visible 'translation missing: xx.key' string. By moving fallback configuration into config/initializers/i18n.rb, fallbacks to the site default locale and English are now active in every environment, including the test suite. This means tests and development rendering that used to fail loudly on incomplete locale files will now silently render English, hiding locale-file regressions (missing/renamed keys) until production-like behavior differs from what was validated. If global fallbacks are intended, consider keeping a way (e.g. raising on missing translations in test) to detect incomplete locale files.
